Lupin Limited and Natco Pharma Limited Receive Approval from U.S. FDA for Eribulin Mesylate Injection
news.body: Lupin Limited and its alliance partner Natco Pharma Limited announced the approval from the United States Food and Drug Administration for Natco's Abbreviated New Drug Application for Eribulin Mesylate Injection, 1 mg/2 mL (0.5 mg/mL) Single-Dose Vials. Eribulin Mesylate Injection, 1 mg/2 mL (0.5 mg/mL) Single-Dose Vials is the bioequivalent to the reference listed drug Halaven Injection of Eisai Inc. Eribulin Mesylate Injection is indicated for the treatment of adults with metastatic breast cancer who have previously received at least two chemotherapeutic regimens for the treatment of metastatic disease and unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma who have received a prior anthracycline-containing regimen. news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS exceeds analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹79.20 (down from ₹105 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹43.8b (down 1.3% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹14.2b (down 25% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 32% (down from 43% in FY 2025). The decrease in margin was primarily driven by higher expenses. Revenue was in line with analyst estimates. Earnings per share (EPS) surpassed analyst estimates by 9.5%. Revenue is expected to decline by 9.7% p.a. on average during the next 2 years, while revenues in the Pharmaceuticals industry in India are expected to grow by 11%. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 19% per year whereas the company’s share price has increased by 17% per year.

news.title: NATCOPHARM: Future Diabetes And Oncology Launches Will Face Softer Expectations
news.body: Analysts have kept the fair value estimate for NATCO Pharma steady at ₹938.10 per share, reflecting unchanged assumptions around discount rate, revenue trends, profit margin and future P/E, and signalling no shift in their overall price target rationale. What's in the News NATCO received Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation approval to manufacture and market generic Semaglutide injection in India, with a launch planned in March 2026 targeting adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes (Key Developments).

news.title: NATCOPHARM: Future Diabetes Launch Will Face Softer Revenue Expectations
news.body: Analysts have revised their price target on NATCO Pharma from ₹982.64 to ₹938.10, citing updated assumptions that reflect softer revenue expectations, a higher projected profit margin and a lower future P/E multiple. What's in the News Launch of generic Semaglutide injection in India planned for March 2026, with multi dose vials priced at MRP of ₹1,290 per month for 2mg/1.5ml and 4mg/3ml, and ₹1,750 for 8mg/3ml, plus pen devices in April 2026 at MRPs of ₹4,000, ₹4,200 and ₹4,500 per month.

news.title: NATCOPHARM: Diabetes Franchise Partnership And Demerger Plan Will Support Future Upside

news.title: NATCOPHARM: Domestic Diabetes Franchise Partnership Will Support Future Upside

What's in the News Eris Lifesciences announced a partnership with NATCO Pharma to commercialise semaglutide in India, combining Eris's diabetes franchise with NATCO's manufacturing and regulatory capabilities for complex formulations (Client Announcement).

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹8.46 (up from ₹7.43 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹7.05b (up 49% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹1.52b (up 14% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 22% (down from 28% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Revenue missed analyst estimates by 8.4%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 2.4%. Revenue is expected to decline by 16% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, while revenues in the Pharmaceuticals industry in India are expected to grow by 10%. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 30% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 15% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.

This reflects fine tuning of their views on revenue declines and profit margins rather than a fundamental shift in the outlook.
